correctness.rationale: The graph is bipartite cubic. In a Hamilton cycle, consecutive distinct lower vertices have a unique common upper vertex if their union is a triple, and none otherwise. Thus a Hamilton tour is recovered exactly from its cyclic lower-vertex order when the ten successive unions are distinct triples. Fixing one lower vertex and one direction per order exhausts the unoriented, unrooted states and gives 24 cycles. For the alternate Petersen representation, label upper vertices by complements of two-sets; containment becomes disjointness. On the cyclic set of ground labels, write A_i={i,i+1}, B_i={i,i+2} mod 5. The A-shell has successive indices 2j mod 5 in alternating layers, with spoke to B_(2j+2) in the opposite layer. The B-shell has successive steps j↦j±3 in this positional numbering, giving GP(10,3). In a cubic graph complementing a Hamilton edge set gives a perfect matching and does not change symmetric differences; an alternating single flip is therefore exactly a connected nonempty degree-two difference. Independent replay /workspace/branches/check_4.py checks all 276 state pairs on the direct Hamilton edge sets; connected difference lengths/counts are 10:84 and 18:60, with all other differences of split shapes (6,6), (6,10), (10,10). Neighbor sets and two-step reachability give (1,7,16) at every vertex, and the length-18 graph has two size-twelve components of degree five. Exceptional edges are exactly those with no common neighbor; their components are six squares, with one neighbor per vertex in each other square, giving all fifteen cross-square perfect matchings. The permutation action is transitive with order-five stabilizer; labelling gH by grg⁻¹ for a chosen stabilizer generator is well-defined and has 24 values, since the centralizer of a five-cycle is its cyclic subgroup. The replay verifies that the square labels are the four generators of one Sylow subgroup and within-square neighbors are the second and third powers. By the normalizer action each cross-square neighbor set is one stabilizer orbit: the order-five subgroup acts transitively on the other five Sylow subgroups. This reproduces the finite conclusions independently of the supplied matching and tour implementations.
residual_risks: The count is of unoriented, unrooted cycles and the move graphs are restricted to Hamiltonian complements; no larger-graph extrapolation is supported.

An order-five vertex stabilizer would fix the two exceptional neighbors, so with the transitive coordinate action of degree 24 this places them inside the same Sylow fiber; thus local structure and symmetry can be very close to the square theorem. The length-18 component count needs more than a total transition count.

checked_sources: Frozen Finding, independent exact pair enumeration and comparison to Ito's unrestricted alternating-cycle model
value.rationale: The natural first nontrivial middle-level state space tests whether alternating swaps can transform Hamilton tours while retaining Hamiltonicity. The sharp smallest usable move length, short-path connectivity and intrinsic organization of the shortest moves into six group-labelled fibers explain the connectivity structure rather than just count states. The deceptively plentiful length-18 moves fail to connect all states, illustrating why length and admissibility matter. These exact results are useful benchmarks for reconfiguration on middle levels and cubic graphs.
residual_risks: The benchmark is confined to this graph and the specified move type; the known state count is not itself the valuable addition.
